content:
Nuevo Laredo’s municipal government is bringing city hall to Colonia Hidalgo today. The “Presidencia Cerquita de Ti” (Your Nearby Presidency) outreach program sets up shop Thursday, October 22, from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at Plaza Libertad — on Gutiérrez Street between Colima and Prolongación Avenida Monterrey — where residents can handle paperwork, request services, and get help without traveling to multiple city offices.

The program, driven by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, installs modules from different municipal departments and participating agencies in a single location. According to the city’s announcement, residents will be able to:

  • Pay property tax (predial), file reports and complaints, and request official documents
  • Receive legal advice, negotiate agreements (convenios), and join social programs
  • Sign up for cultural and sports workshops
  • Access health brigades: general medicine, nutritional guidance, psychological care, and women’s health services
  • Get free screenings for glucose levels, blood pressure, and glycated hemoglobin, plus vaccinations and rapid HIV, VDRL, and hepatitis tests, subject to each service’s availability

Modules from the DIF family-services system, the Civil Registry, the State Fiscal Office, and the Nuevo Laredo College of Notaries will also be on hand with information and guidance on procedures, the city said.

Why it matters

For working families in Colonia Hidalgo, a single trip downtown can cost a day’s wages. Programs like this one are how a city government proves it can reach the neighborhoods — or reveals where it can’t. The measure of success is not the announcement, but the lines: how many residents get seen, how many petitions get answered, and whether the follow-through happens after the tents come down.

title: City Hall Comes to Colonia Hidalgo: Nuevo Laredo's 'Presidencia Cerquita de Ti' Today, 9 a.m.–2 p.m.
